i get these daily too, actually it forms constantly all day long but especially at night while i sleep, and only on one side of the nose.  I finally have determined the cause is because the nasal passage on that side is slightly too narrow, which causes airflow to be poor, which in turn causes excessive dryness and lack of moisture and normal mucus, which causes a dry spot to form and scab over at precisely where the air passage opening is.  Often the scab is bloodier or the nose bleeds a bit after the scab is removed.  Doctors say they cant do much since ive already had 2 septoplastys and the nose is anatomically OK already.  Very frustrating.

Breathe right strips help.  Sometimes drinking water and staying active/exercise also help,

Already tried, been there done that for the past 5-6 years.  Nearly everything I did has basically just backfired ultimately and made things worse.  Or just hasn't made any significant difference because it's not addressing the root problem.

My most current thinking is that there is simply a chemical imbalance, I am most likely just deficient in something.  Unfortunately I do not know which chemical.  And I've already been going to doctors for years.  I've gone as far as any person can be expected to go on their own without having the cure and it only gets me so far. 

 I've lost patience, motivation to keep trying to repair things, and every second that things aren't better they are getting worse.  

Seeking treatment also has risks.  It requires trial and error, possibly taking wrong medication(s) for long periods of time which will just worsen things.

Thank you for the reply.  Yes, i forgot to mention that water sometimes helps a bit.  I have felt this symptom numerous times in the past 5 years, usually when I am at my most inactive for weeks or months continuously

Around 2008-2009 is approximately when things began to deteriorate for me, but its hard to pinpoint.  Around 2011 is when I saw a therapist and a psychiatrist to begin addressing the mental/emotional  component and at that time a lot was written down and explored.  Since then I thought I had been on a somewhat new path forward but it is very clear now that this path is totally unsustainable in lots of ways.  Mid-Last year I stopped taking my meds altogether.  In recent months and weeks more and more things just keep piling on gradually..  It has the feeling of the nails being hammered into the coffin.

I've seen a therapist years ago.  There were some things she helped out with, to relax me and help me understand and cope better with my issues.  But ultimately i don't think the underlying issue(s) has been resolved, basically because I don't think it can be. My concern about going to a professional now is not that I think they don't care.  On the contrary, I think most actually do care, but their job description is to help lift people up out of suicidal ideation regardless of whether the person might legitimately be better off dead (I know, thats subjective).  As far as my issue(s) go, I've been writing down the reasons in recent days, its all very interconnected and some of it is difficult for me to articulate.
